greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. We gather today in the presence of the Lord, seeking the comfort of His Word and the strength of His promise to be with us always.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the seed that falls to the earth to bring forth life: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the leaven that transforms the whole of our lives: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the one who gathers us into your eternal kingdom: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
homily:
We often imagine the Kingdom of God as a grand, finished structure—a cathedral of marble or a city of light. We want to see the blueprints. We want to know exactly how it is built, where the foundations are laid, and when the roof will be placed upon it. But Jesus, in today’s Gospel, turns our eyes away from the grand architecture of the world and points us toward the garden. He tells us that the Kingdom of God is like a mustard seed, the smallest of all seeds, and like a bit of yeast, hidden deep within a large batch of flour. It is not a spectacle. It is a quiet, hidden, almost invisible process. It is a mystery that works from the inside out.

Think of the mustard seed. When a man plants it in his garden, he does not stand over it with a magnifying glass, demanding to see immediate growth. He plants it, and then he waits. He trusts the soil. He trusts the rain. He trusts the God who made the seed and the earth. And in time, in its own way, that tiny, unremarkable speck becomes a large bush. The birds of the sky come and dwell in its branches. It becomes a place of shelter, a place of rest, a place where life can find a home. The growth is not forced; it is organic. It is the natural unfolding of a life that has been planted in the right ground.

Benjamin Vo understood this kind of quiet, deep growth. You remember him—a boy of such extraordinary, brilliant curiosity. He didn't just study math or technology; he lived in the possibilities of them. He had that mind that could navigate the complex logic of cloud infrastructure or the intricate systems of an airplane, but he was always, always tethered to a heart that was growing in kindness. Think of that image of the 'con chim airlines'—that dream he had, the name that made him giggle and smile. It wasn't just a hobby. It was a seed of imagination, a way he was trying to build a bridge between his world and the world of others. He was always planting, always imagining, always looking for ways to connect the people he loved to the things he found beautiful.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has felt like a fallow field. You look at the place where Ben used to be, and you feel the ache of a season that has ended too soon. You wonder about the harvest that was promised but seems to have been cut down. I want to tell you something that is true: nothing is lost in the garden of God. The seed that was Benjamin—his laughter, his brilliant mind, his gentle, empathetic heart—it was not wasted. It was planted. And the growth that he brought into your lives, the love that he shared, the joy that he gave—that is the Kingdom. It is still growing. It is still bearing fruit in ways you cannot yet see. You are not living in a place of death; you are living in a place of deep, hidden, holy growth.

There is a temptation, when we are hurting, to look for a reason for the winter. We want to know why the frost came, why the bloom was cut short. We wonder if we missed a sign, if we could have protected the plant better, if we could have done more to keep the garden green. I want to lift that stone from your hearts today: you missed nothing. You were the gardeners he needed. You provided the soil of love, the sunlight of your attention, and the water of your devotion. You were the ones who sat with him, who listened to his stories, who encouraged his dreams. You did everything that a parent could do, and you did it with a love that was, and is, a reflection of the Father’s own heart. The illness that took him was not a failure of your care. It was not a punishment. It was a sorrow, a tragedy that came from outside, beyond any human control. Do not blame yourselves. Do not carry the weight of 'what if.' You loved him perfectly, and that love is the most fertile ground there is.

In our first reading today, St. Paul speaks of the mystery of the 'one flesh' union between a husband and a wife. He says, 'This is a great mystery, but I speak in reference to Christ and the Church.' He is talking about a love that is so deep, so committed, and so sacrificial that it becomes a single life. That is the kind of love that brought Benjamin into the world. It is the kind of love that binds your family together. When you look at each other, when you lean on each other, when you weep together in the quiet of the night, you are living out that mystery. You are a family of four. That is a reality that is etched into the very fabric of eternity. No distance can break that bond. No death can tear that flesh apart. You are still a family, and you are being held by the same Christ who loves the Church.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the geometry of this love better than anyone. You know the way the house feels, the way the memories are woven into the very fabric of your life together. You are the one who carries the legacy of his joy. When you look at the sky, when you think of the planes, when you remember the games you coded together, you are participating in the growth of the Kingdom. You are a vital part of this family, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who sees the beauty in the small things. You are a witness to the world that love is stronger than any distance, that it is the most beautiful material in the universe.

There is a story about a boy who once offered his entire piggy bank to help an uncle he loved. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it—the offer was the thing. It was the movement of a heart that was already generous, already sacrificial, already looking for ways to be a blessing. That is the heart of your son. That is the heart of your brother. That is the heart that God is shaping in you, too. When you offer your own grief, when you offer your own longing, when you offer your own service to the poor in his name, you are doing exactly what he would have done. You are keeping the love flowing. You are the stewards of his legacy. You are the ones who keep the water moving, just as you have done with the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a sign, a tangible, physical piece of the grace that you are living. It is a sign that the love that was poured into Ben is still flowing, still quenching the thirst of the poor, still bringing life to the dry places. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope, you are adding to that well. You are keeping the water moving. You are ensuring that the legacy of his gentle spirit continues to nourish the earth.

Do you remember how Benjamin used to giggle when he talked about 'con chim airlines'? It was such a beautiful, simple, joyful thing. It was a dream of flight, of rising above the earth, of seeing the world from a different perspective. That is exactly where he is now. He is at the banquet of heaven, and he is looking down at you with that same sweet, gentle smile. He is not worried. He is not suffering. He is in the presence of the One who is the source of all love. And he is waiting for you. He is waiting for you to finish your journey, to keep your lamp lit, to keep your heart open, and to keep loving the way he loved.

We are living in a time that often feels like a long, cold autumn. We see the leaves falling, we feel the air turning, and we are tempted to look for security in the things we can control. But Jesus is inviting us to look at the mustard seed. He is inviting us to trust that the ground we are standing on is holy. He is not distant. He is the one who is kneeling with you in the silence. He is the one who is holding your hand when the night is at its deepest. He is the one who is whispering to your hearts that you are not alone, that you are not forgotten, and that you are loved beyond all measure.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is not a new set of plans. It is a simple, quiet, doable thing: keep your heart open to the cultivation of the Spirit. When you feel the ache, do not turn away from it. Let it be the place where God meets you. When you see someone who is struggling, when you see someone who is thirsty, when you see someone who is just trying to make it through the day, remember that they, too, bear the image of the Creator. Reach out to them. Give a little of your time, a little of your heart, a little of your kindness. Not because you have to, but because you are overflowing with the love that Benjamin left behind. You are the stewards of his legacy. You are the ones who keep the water moving. Every act of mercy, every quiet prayer, every moment of patience is a seed planted in the garden of the Lord. And God, who is the faithful Gardener, will ensure that it grows into something beautiful, something eternal, something that will shelter many.

Do not be afraid of the future. The same God who held Benjamin in his hand as he looked out at the sky is the same God who holds you today as you look out at your own horizon. He is not a stranger. He is your Father. He knows the exact shape of your heart, he knows the depth of your longing, and he knows how much you miss the one you love. And he is promising you that the story is not over. The reunion is certain. Keep your eyes on the sky. Keep your heart in the light. And remember that he is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the banquet is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. You are a family of four, and your story is being written in the book of life, where every page is filled with the grace of God and the beauty of the love you share. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
petition_call: Let us pray to the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who carry the weight of grief and the ache of missing a loved one, that God may console them, strengthen their hearts, and fill them with the hope of the resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Be subordinate to one another out of reverence for Christ.
Wives should be subordinate to their husbands as to the Lord.
For the husband is head of his wife
just as Christ is head of the Church,
he himself the savior of the Body.
As the Church is subordinate to Christ,
so wives should be subordinate to their husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives,
even as Christ loved the Church
and handed himself over for her to sanctify her,
cleansing her by the bath of water with the word,
that he might present to himself the Church in splendor,
without spot or wrinkle or any such thing,
that she might be holy and without blemish.
So also husbands should love their wives as their own bodies.
He who loves his wife loves himself.
For no one hates his own flesh
but rather nourishes and cherishes it,
even as Christ does the Church,
because we are members of his Body.For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother
and be joined to his wife,
and the two shall become one flesh.This is a great mystery,
but I speak in reference to Christ and the Church.
In any case, each one of you should love his wife as himself,
and the wife should respect her husband.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1a) Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Blessed are you who fear the LORD,
who walk in his ways!
For you shall eat the fruit of your handiwork;
blessed shall you be, and favored.
R. Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine
in the recesses of your home;
Your children like olive plants
around your table.
R.  Blessed are those who fear the Lord.
Behold, thus is the man blessed
who fears the LORD.
The LORD bless you from Zion:
may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem
all the days of your life.
R. Blessed are those who fear the Lord.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said, “What is the Kingdom of God like?
To what can I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in the garden.
When it was fully grown, it became a large bush
and the birds of the sky dwelt in its branches.”Again he said, “To what shall I compare the Kingdom of God?
It is like yeast that a woman took
and mixed in with three measures of wheat flour
until the whole batch of dough was leavened.”

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
